_comment: Post-deploy proof that site/wrangler.jsonc is ACTUALLY IN EFFECT in production.

Every expectation below interpolates ${VAR} from wrangler.jsonc's own vars block, so
these assert 'production reflects what THAT FILE declares' rather than re-stating the
values here. Change a var in the config and this probe follows it automatically; if the
config stops being read and the dashboard holds different values, this goes red.
Never add a secret here. SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is a Pages Secret and is asserted
only by its effect (the queue answers instead of 500ing).
_unproven: Nothing. Every var and binding wrangler.jsonc declares is now exercised by a probe above,
and the runner will start naming anything newly declared that is not.
PAGE_FEEDBACK was the last gap and it closed on 2026-07-30. It could not be probed through
the feedback endpoint: functions/api/feedback.ts validates method, encoding, answer, path
shape and the crisis exclusion BEFORE `if (!env.PAGE_FEEDBACK) return 503`, so any request
able to reach that branch also writes a row to the live tally when the binding is present —
and that POST is D1's only consumer. Probing it would have corrupted the one signal the
So the binding was made observable instead of the observer privileged: functions/api/health.ts
serves GET /api/health?deep=1, read-only, no credential, no data disclosed. Same move that
closed the page-repair proxy's Durable Object.

probes.name: auth BFF received KEYCLOAK_* — login redirects to the declared issuer and client
probes.whenMissing: keycloakConfigured() goes false and login.ts answers 404 'sign-in is not configured' — a plausible status that a `status < 500` health check would call green while sign-in is dead for every contributor.

probes.name: auth BFF sets the PKCE/CSRF cookies the callback reads back
probes.whenMissing: a 302 with no cookies means the redirect was manufactured somewhere other than login.ts — the flow would fail at the callback with a state mismatch.

probes.name: contributions Function runs and fails CLOSED (not static-404, not 503)
probes.whenMissing: 404 means the Function did not deploy or its env is absent; 503 means a declared binding did not resolve; a 200/303 would mean the fail-closed guard is gone.

probes.name: contributions Function rejects non-POST explicitly (proves the dispatcher, not asset handling)
probes.whenMissing: a 404 here means static asset handling answered the path — the Function is not deployed at all. This is why the check asserts 405 rather than 'not 5xx'.

probes.name: Functions layer is up (shallow health, touches no binding — a discriminator, not a config check)
probes.whenMissing: a non-200 here means the Functions layer itself is not serving; the deep check below would also fail, for a reason that has nothing to do with the config. Verified in a real Pages runtime with the D1 table absent: this route still answered 200, which is exactly why it is kept separate from the deep one.

probes.name: PAGE_FEEDBACK (D1) resolved — deep binding liveness, read-only, no credential
probes.whenMissing: 503 {"status":"degraded"} naming the binding: "unavailable" means env.PAGE_FEEDBACK was undefined, i.e. the config was not applied to this deployment; "unreachable" means the binding resolved but the query failed — D1 down, or the page_feedback table missing/renamed. Two different faults with two different fixes, deliberately not collapsed into one word. This route runs SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1: it proves the binding AND the schema while reading no tally value and writing nothing.

probes.name: feedback Function is deployed and validating (writes nothing — crisis paths are rejected before the D1 branch)
probes.whenMissing: 404 means the Function did not deploy; 503 'feedback store not configured' would mean the D1 binding did not resolve — but note this probe CANNOT reach that branch, by design. See _unproven below.
